title: Panel synthesis — oddities and calibration (Ellie Mendoza notes)
content:
Context: quick post-panel dump capturing weird signals and calibration notes. Candidate: Eli Sandoval (onsite loop 2025-11-02). Role: Senior Runtime Engineer (latency/cost/infra). This doc is for internal calibration and to highlight items I think the panel should explicitly discuss before vote.

Panel composition: Marco (lead), Devon (SRE), Me (runtime), Nadia was remote (couldn't join live coding).

High-level impression (tl;dr): smart operator, good ownership instincts, borderline depth on kernel-level inference optimizations. Comfortable shipping infra but had inconsistent answers when pressed on attention-optimizations and KV cache semantics.

What stood out (positive):
- Clear prior experience running customer-facing model endpoints at scale (gave concrete rollback story).
- Strong product sense: prioritized predictable latency over micro-cost wins during hypothetical tradeoffs.
- Good communication during system design: sketched a multi-tenant routing policy that handled cold-starts gracefully.

Oddities / red flags:
- Live coding: used an unusual heap-of-strings approach for manipulating KV cache in pseudocode; works but doesn't map to low-level cache pointers we use. Suggests gap in implementation-level experience.
- Quantization knowledge felt patchy. Candidate cited symmetric quantization as default for GPUs — when asked about per-channel asymmetric quant, they deferred. For our work that matters.
- Latency math: initially claimed batching always increases tail latency for small replicas, then later corrected to nuance. The back-and-forth left an impression of shaky intuition under pressure.

Behavioral / culture signals:
- Ownership and escalation: strong examples of owning on-call incidents, proactively wrote postmortems that led to 2 permanent mitigations.
- Collaboration: asked many clarifying questions and invited feedback; would likely fit in small, cross-functional teams.

Concrete scoring (my quick numbers; rough):
- Technical depth: 6/10 (systems-level but not kernel/attn-ops depth)
- Product/ownership: 8/10
- On-call/operational experience: 8/10
- Communication: 7/10
- Overall fit for senior runtime (IC3/4): borderline — leans strong IC3, soft for IC4 given kernel gaps.

Follow-ups / questions for panel to decide:
1) Do we need an IC4 candidate with kernel-level optimization expertise now, or can we hire someone who is a strong operator and grow them into that space?
2) Would a short take-home that focuses on attention/kv cache implementation (not full perf harness) help resolve the quantization/implementation depth uncertainty?
3) Should we ask engineering hiring to loop in a repo owner from serving-runtime for a quick 30m technical calibration?

Suggested next steps (my recommendation):
- Move candidate to a short, focused take-home (2–4 hours) that asks for: a) a small design for a KV cache invalidation scheme with correctness notes, and b) a short write-up on quantization tradeoffs for 8-bit inference on Ampere vs Hopper GPUs.
- If they decline take-home, optional short pairing session with Marco to watch implementation approach (30–45m).

Calibration notes (for archive):
- Marco emphasized we value operational judgement highly; if this hire is for immediate ownership of Dedicated fleets, kernel gaps are a risk.
- Devon flagged that candidate's on-call stories suggest good maturity handling escalations — high value.
- I want to avoid over-penalizing for on-the-spot quantization terminology; practical experience is more telling.

Open questions I still have (notes to self):
- Verify candidate's PR history touching cuBLAS/cuDNN or Triton kernels? (look at GH handle they provided)
- Did candidate's rollback story include measurable postmortem action items? Ask for the link.

Raw scores (for internal vote tally): technical=6, ownership=8, comms=7, overall_recommendation="proceed-to-takehome"

Tiny checklist for next steps:
- [ ] Send take-home prompt + 5-day window
- [ ] Ask candidate for GH links and on-call postmortem
- [ ] Optional pairing slot: book Marco 11/10 10–10:45 PT if candidate accepts

Notes-to-self: keep this draft in users/ until we see take-home results; will move to shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/candidates if we advance.

End of dump.
